title: Duck typing and shape-based APIs
hook: Duck typing and shape-based APIs shows up in everyday JavaScript and in senior interviews — this page explains what it is, why it matters, and how it behaves in the engine versus C# or TypeScript.

blocks.text: Duck typing and shape-based APIs is a core concept in JavaScript (ECMAScript). At run time, the engine enforces behavior dynamically — there is no compile step unless you add TypeScript on top. This page explains the idea in plain English first, then shows small, explained examples you can run in the browser console or Node.js.

entries.plainDefinition: The official specification that JavaScript implements. TypeScript is a typed superset that compiles to ECMAScript.
entries.example: const, classes, and async/await are ECMAScript features.

blocks.text: Senior interviews and production code both probe whether you understand Duck typing and shape-based APIs beyond syntax memorization. Misunderstanding here leads to subtle bugs — wrong equality results, leaked memory, untyped JSON boundaries, or async ordering surprises. If you know C#, the comparison sections below help you transfer mental models instead of starting from zero.

blocks.title: Interview trap
blocks.body: Interviewers often ask "Duck typing and shape-based APIs" as a follow-up to a coding exercise. They want mechanism and tradeoffs — not a one-line definition.

blocks.title: Duck typing and shape-based APIs across languages
Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Treating Duck typing and shape-based APIs as pure syntax without run-time behavior. Skipping validation at JSON or API boundaries. Saying "it works on my machine" without noting browser versus Node differences.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: add logging or DevTools breakpoints around Duck typing and shape-based APIs, write a failing test that captures the edge case, and explain tradeoffs aloud in design review. Senior interviewers want mechanism — what the engine does — plus when not to use the clever version.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Hand-waving "Duck typing and shape-based APIs just works" without mentioning run-time checks, error paths, or comparison to C# and TypeScript. Cannot trace a concrete bug to this concept.
